title: SuspendUser
description: The body of an administrative suspension, derived from identity_application::administration::SuspendUser. `reason` is a non-Option String, and that is the enforcement: a suspension without a stated reason is one nobody can appeal.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; SuspendUserCommand has no body and no route serves it

context.description: Who is asking, and under which session. Required at AAL2.

reason.description: Why, recorded in the audit trail. MANDATORY and non-empty — the type carries a plain String, not an Option<String>, and the crate has a test recording that a future Option<String> would be a regression. It is CLIENT-SAFE: the reason is operator prose, never a secret and never a platform error string.
reason.x-test: identity_application::administration::tests::a_suspension_requires_a_reason asserts the serialised body carries reason as a non-null string, and the test comment records that this is enforced by the TYPE rather than by a validation branch

x-effect-is-not-complete-when-this-retur: Suspension also revokes the user's sessions server-side, so the effect is not finished when the call returns. The client returns void for exactly this reason: a screen must report what the Worker said, not what it assumed. `status` remains the authoritative gate even so — a stale session must still be refused.
x-a-client-may-omit-the-reason: The operator console's client makes `reason` optional at its own boundary, and says why: an operator suspending someone mid-incident should not be blocked by a form, and the audit record's value does not depend on it. That is a UI decision about whether to PROMPT. The server-side contract above keeps the field mandatory, and a console that omits it will be refused.

x-refusals.last-active-administrator: ApplicationError::Domain — a suspension of the last active administrator is refused
